## Working practices

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#working-practices))

- One command per invocation: no bundled steps (`a && b; c`), except a genuine pipeline or a tight
  pair where the join is the point.
- Exit status: never mask a command's exit status. The command under test runs bare and last in
  its invocation, since the Bash tool reports a nonzero exit, with `set -o pipefail` first when it
  is piped. No `&&` after a piped stage, no trailing `; echo "exit=$?"`. To report and still fail:
  `cmd || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }`.
- Long output: the Bash tool returns only part of a long output, and the part it drops may hold
  the result. A validation, build, or test run, an unbounded log or diff, each command `custom.md`
  names, and any command whose length is in doubt runs as
  `set -o pipefail; <command> 2>&1 | tee tmp/last.log | tail -25`. A pass is the exit status, so
  nothing runs again to see one, and a failure is read from the file, the slice it needs.
- Hooks: the Claude Code hooks are in `agent-data/` and `bash agent-data/hooks.sh install`, the
  user's to run, puts them in `~/.claude/hooks/` and registers them in `~/.claude/settings.json`.
  `bash-guard.sh` denies the two masks it can see, an echo of `$?` or `PIPESTATUS` and a `cargo`
  or `vc-x1` command piped into `tail`, `head`, `grep`, or `rg` without `pipefail`. `bash-allow.sh`
  skips the prompt for `cargo`, `jj`, and `vc-x1`, and `inhibit-sleep.sh` keeps the machine awake
  while a session works.
- Scratch files: where a thing goes is decided by whether it can be reproduced.
  - `tmp/`: disposable, cleared at any time, gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand. `/tmp` is for
    out-of-project temporaries.
  - `tmp-durable/`, gitignored beside it: what we would rather not lose and can reproduce, a built
    index for one.
  - `notes/`: what must last, committed and pushed. It holds no pointer into `tmp-durable/`.
  - Code set aside: a jj commit with a local bookmark, not pushed, so either of us can address it,
    never a patch file.
- Slice reads: read the slice you need from long notes files. The acquaint read is `TODO.md`
  `offset=0, limit=60` ([notes.md](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
- https remotes: use https remotes, and check for an ssh remote first when a push dies at the
  network leg. A remote URL change needs the user's go.
- Delegate: mechanical subtasks go to lesser models (Opus/Haiku/Sonnet).
- No memory directory: `~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/` is unused, the agent-files are.
- Speculation: mark it in durable text with "We think ..." ([Speculation
  marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker)).
- Plain synopsis: end a technical explanation in conversation with one, marked "The plain version:"
  ([Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations)).

### A session's rules are its own agent-files

A session's rules are the agent-files of the project it started in, and its `custom.md`, and rules
living in any other repo are ignored unless these files or the user direct otherwise
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)). So another repo's own
protocol (a shared store's README, another project's agent-files) governs a write to it only as
far as the delegation reaches, and this file's conduct rules, the step reads, the reviews, the
per-push approval, and the stops, bind every commit and push the session makes, in any repo,
cycle or not. A repo with a live agent of its own is not written at all: message its agent.

### Stop and ask

Stop and ask on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes on a
simple task has produced no progress ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#stop-and-ask)).

## Changing the agent-files

A new repo starts from an adopter's set, its working copy's by default, applied by
`scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh`, and every adopter carries its own copy
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

- Local experiments: a local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment, diffed against the copy it
  started from while the rules are being tried. After the experiment there may be a proposal.
- Proposing: a proposal is one set of diffs, to the rules or beyond them, that an adopter may or
  may not accept as is.
- Convergence: the adopter reviews the diff between the proposal and its files and accepts it as is
  or proposes changes. It is a negotiation whose goal is everyone accepting the same thing, and
  that goal is not a requirement.
- Acceptance: the adopter and the proposer agree on the contents, identical or not.
- Retirement: a resolved experiment retires like a finished Todo, adopted and rejected alike: the
  cycle that resolved it is its record.

## CONTRIBUTING.md

The work-repo's [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) is the project's layer, committed, so every
clone carries it, and `vc-dr-apply` starts one ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#contributingmd)).
Two headings are fixed, since the agent-files find them by name:
[Tasks](CONTRIBUTING.md#tasks) names the commands that build, test, and install the work, and
[Agents](CONTRIBUTING.md#agents) is what an agent working there reads beyond the agent-files, read
at acquaint after `custom.md`, which overrides it.

## custom.md

When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent must read it first, and it overrides
anything in the agent-files and `CONTRIBUTING.md` ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). It is
the place for what is local to the workspace, one machine's paths and permissions, since a change
every clone needs is a cycle on the agent-file it belongs in, or on `CONTRIBUTING.md` when it is the
project's alone. The session lock,
[session-lock.md](agent-data/session-lock.md), is an experiment it may carry.

Two commands, in this order:

```
jj bookmark track feat-one-cycle-flow-plan-rungs-close --remote=origin
jj new feat-one-cycle-flow-plan-rungs-close
```

The first makes the local bookmark from the remote one and tracks it. The second puts an empty `@` on its tip, so the bookmark sits on `@-`, which is where `vc-x1-dev cycle status` expects it.

Earlier in this session I did it the other way round (`jj new feat-one-cycle-flow-plan-rungs-close@origin`, then the track), which ends in the same state. If that still holds after your sync, there is nothing to redo, and `jj st` will show the bookmark on the parent commit.

After that, `cargo xtask install` gives you a `vc-x1-dev` built from the branch, which the cycle's commands need.

The plain version: track the remote bookmark, then `jj new` on it.

From ~/tmp/t85-22 while testing multi-step:
- The schema header `vc-x1 config` prints still says "run `vc-x1 config --validate`",
  which was retired at 0.80.6 in favour of `vc-x1 validate-config`, but actually
  `config --validate` is more correct with our current style where we want to retire
  hyphenated commands.

### A parked head is durable and continues on any machine

(wink + agent, 2026-11-10, 15, and 16) A cycle's work sometimes waits off its chain, a rung's edits
set aside for an unplanned rung, or a cycle stopped for the night. Each is a head beside the
cycle's, a bushiness with a cost, worth it once the head is durable, on the remote, and continued on
this machine or another. Merged from **feat: cycle sets a rung's edits aside and takes them back**
and **Work in progress is durable and continues on any machine** (wink, 2026-11-16).

- **The set-aside** (wink + agent, 2026-11-15, from **fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current**).
  Unplanned work sets the next rung's edits aside as a jj commit with a local bookmark, and that
  cycle did it by hand: `jj restore` of the version files, `jj commit`, `jj bookmark create`, and
  `jj new` on the cycle's tip, with a `jj rebase` and a bookmark delete to take them back. The hand
  bookmark is what found the branch revset's bug, so the tool should own the steps.
  - `cycle --set-aside` saves the working copy as a commit under a local bookmark, leaves the
    version and record files out so the return cannot conflict on them, and puts `@` back on the
    cycle's tip.
  - `cycle --take-back` rebases it onto the new tip and deletes the bookmark.
  - The names follow the stage flags and are to be settled at the opening.
- **Work in progress** (wink, 2026-11-10). A cycle stopped for the night was made durable by a work
  and an agent commit titled `wip`, pushed, and removing them took two abandons and two backward
  pushes by `jj`, since `vc-x1 push` would fold the agent `@` into the last rung's agent commit. A
  scheme is wanted that makes work in progress durable, on the remote, and easy to continue on this
  machine or another, then leaves no trace in the cycle's history once the rung it belongs to is
  committed.
  - We think a separate ref, a `wip/<bookmark>` on the remote holding both `@`s, is the shape: the
    cycle's bookmark and the agent `main` never move for it, and a `continue` fetches it into `@`.
  - What the other machine's session reads is part of it: the continuation notes ride in the work
    `@` and the transcript in the agent `@`.
- **One mechanism**: name, push, fetch, take back. A parked head changes, rebased when taken back,
  so its ref is a remote bookmark, durable until deleted, not a tag, named for its cycle,
  `aside/<cycle bookmark>` or `wip/<cycle bookmark>`, and its take-back deletes it locally and on
  the remote, a push. No agent commit names a parked head until it lands through a rung.
- Once **feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable** lands, a hand set-aside no
  longer cuts the cycle's branch, and its `--status` reports a parked head as parked, not forked.

### feat: a cycle takes an added bookmark

(wink + agent, 2026-11-16, from **feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable**)
`--bookmark <new>` would add a bookmark beside the cycle's own, which `--bookmark-rename` renames.
Left out of that cycle: each added bookmark invites a head off the cycle's chain, a head an agent
commit names must be made durable, and the record's change ids already address every rung. When a
need appears, it settles whether an added bookmark stays where it is made or advances, whether a
draft push carries it, and whether the Land deletes it.

### feat: vc-x1 delete removes a workspace from this machine

(wink + agent, 2026-11-21, from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close**, wanted soon) Every
test of a cycle makes a workspace by `vc-x1 init --test-repo`, its two repos, its symlink in
`~/.claude/projects/`, and two bare repos under the test-repo directory, and nothing removes them,
so `~/tmp` and the symlinks pile up and each is removed by hand, where a slip deletes a real repo.

- **Solution**: `vc-x1 delete` removes the workspace's local repos and its symlink, and, asked
  for, the local bare repos its remotes are, never a remote reached by a URL.
- **Acceptance check**: a workspace made by `init --test-repo <DIR>` is removed whole by `vc-x1
  delete`, the bare repos with them when asked, and one whose remotes are GitHub's keeps them,
  `delete` removing only what is on this machine.
- **Test repos only, never real ones** (wink, 2026-11-21): a remote whose `origin` is a local path,
  a bare repo as `init --test-repo` makes it, is deleted only when asked, a flag such as
  `--test-repos`, its name open, and a remote reached by a URL, GitHub's or any host's, is never
  touched, as the design below already says.
- The design is **Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands**'s `#### delete removes a
  workspace from this machine` and `#### What stops delete and rename`: the prompt listing what
  goes and the commits found nowhere else, uncommitted or unpushed work refusing, and commits no
  bookmark reaches and a half-made workspace each asking a yes. This entry moves delete ahead of
  that entry's `init` work, wink's order there being `init`, then delete, then rename.

(wink + agent, 2026-11-21, from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close**) After a local Land
the work `main` shows the Land, ahead of origin, and the agent `main` does only sometimes. The Land
moves it when it commits the agent `@` as the partner (`src/land.rs`, `bookmark_set("main", "@-")`),

1744	From ~/tmp/t85-22 while testing multi-step:
1745	- The schema header `vc-x1 config` prints still says "run `vc-x1 config --validate`",
1746	  which was retired at 0.80.6 in favour of `vc-x1 validate-config`, but actually

1750	### A parked head is durable and continues on any machine
1751	
1752	(wink + agent, 2026-11-10, 15, and 16) A cycle's work sometimes waits off its chain, a rung's edits
1753	set aside for an unplanned rung, or a cycle stopped for the night. Each is a head beside the
1754	cycle's, a bushiness with a cost, worth it once the head is durable, on the remote, and continued on
1755	this machine or another. Merged from **feat: cycle sets a rung's edits aside and takes them back**
1756	and **Work in progress is durable and continues on any machine** (wink, 2026-11-16).
1757	
1758	- **The set-aside** (wink + agent, 2026-11-15, from **fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current**).
1759	  Unplanned work sets the next rung's edits aside as a jj commit with a local bookmark, and that
1760	  cycle did it by hand: `jj restore` of the version files, `jj commit`, `jj bookmark create`, and
1761	  `jj new` on the cycle's tip, with a `jj rebase` and a bookmark delete to take them back. The hand
1762	  bookmark is what found the branch revset's bug, so the tool should own the steps.
1763	  - `cycle --set-aside` saves the working copy as a commit under a local bookmark, leaves the
1764	    version and record files out so the return cannot conflict on them, and puts `@` back on the
1765	    cycle's tip.
1766	  - `cycle --take-back` rebases it onto the new tip and deletes the bookmark.
1767	  - The names follow the stage flags and are to be settled at the opening.
1768	- **Work in progress** (wink, 2026-11-10). A cycle stopped for the night was made durable by a work
1769	  and an agent commit titled `wip`, pushed, and removing them took two abandons and two backward
1770	  pushes by `jj`, since `vc-x1 push` would fold the agent `@` into the last rung's agent commit. A
1771	  scheme is wanted that makes work in progress durable, on the remote, and easy to continue on this
1772	  machine or another, then leaves no trace in the cycle's history once the rung it belongs to is
1773	  committed.
1774	  - We think a separate ref, a `wip/<bookmark>` on the remote holding both `@`s, is the shape: the
1775	    cycle's bookmark and the agent `main` never move for it, and a `continue` fetches it into `@`.
1776	  - What the other machine's session reads is part of it: the continuation notes ride in the work
1777	    `@` and the transcript in the agent `@`.
1778	- **One mechanism**: name, push, fetch, take back. A parked head changes, rebased when taken back,
1779	  so its ref is a remote bookmark, durable until deleted, not a tag, named for its cycle,
1780	  `aside/<cycle bookmark>` or `wip/<cycle bookmark>`, and its take-back deletes it locally and on
1781	  the remote, a push. No agent commit names a parked head until it lands through a rung.
1782	- Once **feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable** lands, a hand set-aside no
1783	  longer cuts the cycle's branch, and its `--status` reports a parked head as parked, not forked.

1791	need appears, it settles whether an added bookmark stays where it is made or advances, whether a
1792	draft push carries it, and whether the Land deletes it.

### feat: lookup says what it searched

(wink + agent, 2026-11-21, from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close**) `vc-x1 lookup --line
abc.txt:1`, in a fresh `init` workspace whose `abc.txt` was written by hand and committed by `rung
commit -s w --title`, printed `partner nopttlrpxvmp` and `write none found: no Write, Edit, or Bash
call on abc.txt carries the line`. The partner was the agent `@`, not committed and empty, and the
message reads the same whether the partner holds no session data or holds sessions that never
wrote the line, so the reader cannot weigh it.

- **Solution**: `lookup` says what it searched, facts alone: the partner's state, `partner
  nopttlrpxvmp (the agent @, not committed yet)`, and for no write `write none found: the partner
  holds no session data`, or `write none found: N entries searched, no Write, Edit, or Bash call on
  abc.txt carries the line`.
- **Acceptance check**: in a workspace made by `init --test-repo`, a line written by hand and
  committed `-s w`, `-s b`, and `-s w` then `commit -s a --covers` gets each of the three forms
  as its partner stands, and a line an agent session wrote still gets its window and write.
- **No claim of authorship** (wink, 2026-11-21): even a partner with no session data does not show
  the line was not an agent's, which may have run in another workspace, by a script it ran, or by
  a tool outside Claude Code, so `lookup` never says who wrote a line, only what it found.
- **A later session in the same partner**: committed by `-s a` or the push after the work commit,
  the partner may hold sessions that ran after it, and a write of the same text there is marked
  `(after the window, a later amend)` today, flagged and not the line's origin. Whether to say so
  more plainly is open.

### feat: a cycle is taken up on another machine by one command

(wink + agent, 2026-11-21, from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close**) A cycle draft-pushed
from one machine is continued on another by hand, and the steps are easy to forget: after `vc-x1
sync -s b` the cycle's bookmark is on the remote alone, the work `@` is on `main`, and `cycle
status` and `sync --bookmark` are refused until `jj bookmark track <bookmark> --remote=origin` and
`jj new <bookmark>` are typed, the dev build installed after them. This cycle's closing was taken
up that way, wink asking the agent for the commands. A fresh `vc-x1 clone` leaves the same state.

- **Solution**, provisional: one command, on `sync` or `clone` or of its own, tracks the cycle's
  remote bookmark, puts the work `@` on its tip, and says the dev build is the install task's to
  make, the agent `main` already carrying the session.
- **Acceptance check**, provisional: a cycle draft-pushed from one workspace is taken up in a
  second, synced or freshly cloned, by the one command, and `cycle status` there names the
  bookmark on the work `@-`, its ladder, and the next rung.
- **Which cycle**, open: the remote may hold several draft bookmarks, so the command takes the
  bookmark's name, or lists the remote bookmarks `main@origin` does not reach when given none.
- **`sync` says so**, open: a bare `sync -s b` reports both repos up to date while a draft
  bookmark waits untracked, and it could name each one.
- **A parked head is durable and continues on any machine** is the same need for work not yet
  committed, its `continue` fetching a `wip/` ref, and **clone takes -b for the work-repo's
  bookmark** the same for a clone. The three may be one cycle.
